text:
karla: Heads up — we just got a DSAR from a user asking for deletion + proof of deletion for an account's chat history and any derived embeddings. They specifically call out a backup that was taken 2024-11-03 and say an external contractor had read access earlier this year. Can we confirm what lives where and what we can provide as cryptographic proof?

mike: I can map the data paths. Likely touched: embeddings-store (vectors-bucket), search-cache (memcached snapshot), and s3 snapshots in s3://redwood-prod-backups/embeddings/2024-11-03 encrypted with arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111:key/key-prod-1.

sam: Important: snapshots are immutable. We can remove user records from the live index and mark snapshot objects for deletion on the lifecycle rule, but if snapshot has already been copied to glacier/archival or exported to partner account that's a complication. Any legal hold? @jessica?

jessica: No legal hold currently on that subject. They included a signed request. We need an audit trail that shows deletion actions and ideally checksums of removed objects or a signed statement from our system saying object IDs X,Y,Z were purged. Also confirm who had access (contractor) and whether that access is covered by existing DPA.

karla: Contractor access is the reason they demanded deletion. There was an RBAC change on 2024-06-12 that granted contractor role read:list on backups for two weeks. Need to surface who made that change.

sam: I can pull IAM changes. Quick check: 
```
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=PutRolePolicy --start-time 2024-06-01 --end-time 2024-06-30
```
should show policy updates. I'll take it.

mike: On deletion mechanics: for embeddings-store we have a per-tenant deletion API that removes vectors and triggers a tombstone in the index. For S3 snapshots we need to delete the specific objects and then rotate snapshot manifest. If object is encrypted with key-prod-1 and key has been rotated, we still have key material to decrypt (AWS keeps previous key versions unless key is scheduled for deletion). If key was scheduled for deletion that could complicate proving deletion.

jessica: We need to provide proof to the requester, so please collect: 1) export of audit logs showing delete API call + who triggered it, 2) list of object keys deleted and their SHA256 hashes prior to deletion, 3) KMS key IDs used for those objects, 4) snapshot manifest update showing removal.

karla: Agreed. Action items: @mike run the deletion job for the subject (if no hold), @sam gather RBAC change history + CloudTrail, @mike produce hashes and manifest diff, @jessica will verify legal angle and confirm response wording. ETA 48h? :hourglass_flowing_sand:

mike: I'll spin up the deletion run in a dry-run first and paste logs. Dry-run command: 
```
redwood-cli dsar process --subject-id user_98765 --mode dry-run --components embeddings,search,snapshots
```
I will capture output and hashing: it emits `deleted_objects.json` with pre-delete SHA256.

audit-bot: Runbook link: https://intra.redwood/runbooks/dsar-delete-checklist. Automations: when `--confirm` flag used it pushes an audit event `dsar.delete.confirmed` to the org-audit stream.

sam: FYI on KMS — I checked key-prod-1: there was a rotation on 2024-09-02, but not scheduled for deletion. AWS log shows GenerateDataKey calls for the snapshots on 2024-11-03. We can include the KMS key id and envelope metadata in the audit pack.

mike: Dry-run output snippet: 
```
[INFO] found 37 vector objects for user_98765
[INFO] computed SHA256 for 37 objects -> sha_list.json
[INFO] snapshots to update: s3://redwood-prod-backups/embeddings/2024-11-03/manifest.json
```
Looks straightforward. Will run with `--confirm` after we double-check RBAC history.

karla: One edge case: the requester also asked that we remove any derived embeddings that might appear in cached search results on partner indexer (partner-fed copies). Do we have replication to partner accounts?

sam: There was a one-off export to partner-account:222 on 2024-12-01 (ad-hoc data help). We need to check S3 Replication rules and if an export happened. If so, we must coordinate with partner to delete. I'll open ticket to contact partner security.

jessica: If partner rejects deletion request we need to escalate. For our response to the subject, state what we control and confirm we're engaging third parties and will update within 30 days per GDPR. Keep language measured.

mike: Running the confirmed deletion now (starting): 
```
redwood-cli dsar process --subject-id user_98765 --mode confirmed --components embeddings,search,snapshots
```
Submitting job id job-20240115-0922.

mike: Deletion job completed (partial). Removed 37 vectors, updated manifest, scheduled S3 objects for immediate delete (lifecycle), cleared search-cache entries. Attached: /var/logs/dsar/job-20240115-0922.log (I'll attach audit bundle).

karla: Can you publish an audit bundle to the requester's secure channel and also to legal? The bundle should include cloudtrail snippets for the delete calls and the pre-delete sha_list.json signed by our org key.

audit-bot: Audit bundle created: s3://org-audit-bundles/dsar/user_98765/job-20240115-0922/bundle.zip (ACL: legal-only, requester-signed-link expires in 14 days). Event: dsar.delete.confirmed logged at 1995012398.

sam: RBAC note: CloudTrail shows RBAC change that granted contractor role was created by ben.service (service account) via a deploy on 2024-06-12. Access window was 2024-06-12..2024-06-26. I'll add that snippet to the bundle.

jessica: Good. I'll draft the response: confirm items deleted, include bundle link, state partner checks are in progress, and offer escalation path. Will add: if they need cryptographic proof longer-term we can provide signed SHA256 list valid for 90 days.

karla: Sounds good. Closing loop: document this as a retention-exception advisory in the security playbook so we remember the partner-export edge case. Thanks team. :white_check_mark:

mike: marking thread resolved but will ping if partner asks to retain anything.

jessica: Sending final reply to requester now.

karla: closing — file a short incident note for the RBAC lapse and add remediation to avoid ad-hoc export without partner agreement.
